newsitem.title: USA: US bull market to last yr or two more - strategist.
newsitem.headline: US bull market to last yr or two more - strategist.

text.p: The U.S. bull market that began in 1981 will last for another year or two, according to Michael Hughes, managing director and global market strategist at BZW, the investment banking division of Barclays Bank.

Speaking to reporters in New York, Hughes said, "The long-term bull market that has been in place since 1981 isn't over and won't be until the Dow (Jones Industrial Average) begins with an eight, instead of a six or a seven."
The Dow finished near 6955 on Monday.
The engine for the phase of the bull market that began in 1992 was the decline in bond yields which resulted in a reduction in the cost of capital to companies, Hughes said.
"We've now been in a period of tight fiscal policy with slack monetary policy and that should continue through the next year or two," he said.

Regarding the potential for slightly higher U.S. interest rates, Hughes said "getting the interest-rate correction out of the way" would contribute to a sense of relief and act as a trigger for investors to go back into the U.S. equity market.
"The U.S. is the world's best emerging market," he said, citing America's strength in "knowledge-intensive" industries like media, healthcare and technology.
Hughes said European bond markets have not discounted the risks of monetary union and said the "shakeout" in European bonds that has taken place in recent weeks has a way to go.
"Investors should want to be paid for the risks involved around monetary union," he said.
In terms of actual emerging markets, Hughes said he wanted less exposure to those markets in a time of a turndown in global liquidity.
"Global liquidity is turning down even before interest rates have started to rise," said Hughes. "This is unusual and is occurring because Japan is not contributing," he said.
